meaning: Signal to a vehicle to make it stop.
easyEnglish: Signal to a vehicle to make it stop.
japanese: 合図して、車を止める。
cue: You need a taxi in the street.
reply: Let's flag down a taxi on the main road.
transferCue: Describe getting help on a quiet road.
transferReply: We flagged down a passing van.
nuance: Separable: flag it down. Only for vehicles, and it implies a visible arm signal.
contrast: Flag down stops a vehicle; pull over is the driver stopping at the side.

meaning: Draw attention to something so people notice it.
easyEnglish: Draw attention to something so people notice it.
japanese: 気づいてもらえるよう、指摘しておく。
cue: You spotted a risk that others may miss. Raise it.
reply: I wanted to flag up the licence renewal before March.
transferCue: Describe what a reviewer did with a draft.
transferReply: She flagged up two sections that needed sources.
nuance: Separable: flag it up. British and common at work; American English says flag or raise.
contrast: Flag up raises something for attention; point out corrects a specific fact.

meaning: Stop rising or falling and become level.
easyEnglish: Stop rising or falling and become level.
japanese: 上下の動きが止まり、横ばいになる。
cue: A growth curve has stopped climbing. Describe it.
reply: Growth flattened out after the second quarter.
transferCue: Describe a mountain road.
transferReply: The path flattens out after the treeline.
nuance: Intransitive. Used for graphs, roads and trends alike.
contrast: Flatten out becomes level; level off is an equally common alternative.

meaning: Get rid of someone with an excuse instead of helping.
easyEnglish: Get rid of someone with an excuse instead of helping.
japanese: 言い訳でごまかして、あしらう。
cue: A customer got three different excuses. Describe it.
reply: They fobbed her off with a promise to call back.
transferCue: Insist on a real answer.
transferReply: I don't want to be fobbed off again.
nuance: Separable: fob them off. With introduces the excuse. Always critical.
contrast: Fob off dismisses with an excuse; brush off dismisses without one.

meaning: Behave playfully instead of being serious.
easyEnglish: Behave playfully instead of being serious.
japanese: まじめにやらず、ふざける。
cue: Two people are joking during a safety briefing. Ask them to stop.
reply: Let's not fool around until the briefing is over.
transferCue: Describe a relaxed afternoon.
transferReply: We fooled around with the camera for an hour.
nuance: Intransitive; with introduces what you play with. British English also says fool about.
contrast: Fool around is playful time-wasting; mess up is actually spoiling something.

meaning: Pay a lot of money, usually unwillingly.
easyEnglish: Pay a lot of money, usually unwillingly.
japanese: しぶしぶ大金を払う。
cue: A repair cost far more than expected. React.
reply: We had to fork out three hundred for the boiler.
transferCue: Describe the cost of a concert ticket.
transferReply: People forked out a fortune for those seats.
nuance: Informal; for introduces what you paid for. Always implies reluctance.
contrast: Fork out stresses the amount; cough up stresses the reluctance.

meaning: Spoil something by doing it badly.
easyEnglish: Spoil something by doing it badly.
japanese: へまをして、台なしにする。
cue: A booking error affected a whole trip. Own it.
reply: I fouled up the dates and we lost the deposit.
transferCue: Describe a delivery problem.
transferReply: The courier fouled up the address again.
nuance: Separable: foul it up. Informal; the noun is a foul-up, written with a hyphen.
contrast: Foul up spoils through error; mess up is the more everyday word.

meaning: Make something available that was being used.
easyEnglish: Make something available that was being used.
japanese: ふさがっていたものを、使える状態にする。
cue: Cancelling a meeting creates time. Describe the gain.
reply: Dropping that call frees up an hour on Thursday.
transferCue: Describe reorganising storage.
transferReply: Moving the boxes freed up the whole corner.
nuance: Separable: free it up. Used for time, space, money and people.
contrast: Free up makes a resource available; clear out empties a space entirely.

meaning: Deliberately exclude someone from a group.
easyEnglish: Deliberately exclude someone from a group.
japanese: 意図的に、仲間はずれにする。
cue: A colleague stopped being invited to things. Describe it.
reply: They froze him out after the disagreement.
transferCue: Describe a company losing access to a market.
transferReply: Smaller firms were frozen out of the bidding.
nuance: Separable: freeze them out. Freeze is irregular: froze, frozen. It implies deliberate exclusion.
contrast: Freeze out excludes socially; crowd out squeezes something aside by volume.

meaning: Join together against one person.
easyEnglish: Join together against one person.
japanese: 徒党を組んで、一人を攻撃する。
cue: Several people criticised one colleague at once. Describe it.
reply: It felt like everyone ganged up on her.
transferCue: Describe children playing unfairly.
transferReply: They ganged up on the youngest again.
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces the target. Always disapproving.
contrast: Gang up is many against one; close ranks is a group defending itself.

meaning: Worry someone persistently.
easyEnglish: Worry someone persistently.
japanese: 気がかりが、じわじわ心を苛む。
cue: A small doubt has stayed with you all week. Describe it.
reply: The question has been gnawing at me since Monday.
transferCue: Describe lingering guilt.
transferReply: It gnawed at him until he finally apologised.
nuance: Inseparable; the worry is the subject. Usually in the continuous form.
contrast: Gnaw at is persistent worry; dwell on is choosing to keep thinking about something.

meaning: Wear away someone's resistance or spirit over time.
easyEnglish: Wear away someone's resistance or spirit over time.
japanese: 時間をかけて、気力をすり減らす。
cue: A long dispute has exhausted someone. Describe it.
reply: Two years of appeals will grind anyone down.
transferCue: Describe a demanding commute.
transferReply: The daily travel grinds you down eventually.
nuance: Separable: grind them down. The cause is the subject. Grind is irregular (ground), which reads the same as the noun, so the base form is clearer.
contrast: Grind down exhausts resistance; wear out exhausts energy.

meaning: Try hard to get something, or try to harm someone.
easyEnglish: Try hard to get something, or try to harm someone.
japanese: ねらって全力で動く。人を攻撃しようとする。
cue: A colleague is openly pursuing a promotion. Describe it.
reply: She's gunning for the lead role this year.
transferCue: Describe a rival team's intent.
transferReply: They'll be gunning for us after last season.
nuance: Inseparable and informal, usually in the continuous. For a goal it is neutral; for a person it is hostile.
contrast: Gun for pursues aggressively; go for is a plain choice or attempt.

meaning: Pass something to each person in a group.
easyEnglish: Pass something to each person in a group.
japanese: その場の全員に、順に配る。
cue: You have brought food to share at a meeting.
reply: Could you hand round the biscuits while I pour?
transferCue: Describe distributing documents.
transferReply: She handed round the agenda before we started.
nuance: Separable: hand them round. British; American English says hand around.
contrast: Hand round gives to everyone present; hand out can be to a wider group.

meaning: Remind you of something from the past.
easyEnglish: Remind you of something from the past.
japanese: 過去のことを思い起こさせる。
cue: A new design resembles an older era. Describe it.
reply: The lettering harks back to 1930s posters.
transferCue: Describe a colleague who often mentions the past.
transferReply: He harks back to how things were before the merger.
nuance: Inseparable and slightly formal. About people it can be mildly critical of nostalgia.
contrast: Hark back to evokes the past; look back on is deliberately reviewing it.

meaning: Surround someone so they cannot move freely.
easyEnglish: Surround someone so they cannot move freely.
japanese: 取り囲んで、動きを封じる。
cue: Rules leave a team almost no choices. Describe the feeling.
reply: The conditions hem us in on every side.
transferCue: Describe a narrow valley.
transferReply: The village is hemmed in by steep hills.
nuance: Separable but very often passive: be hemmed in by. Used for geography and for constraints.
contrast: Hem in surrounds and confines; box in blocks the way out of a specific space.

meaning: Depend entirely on one thing.
easyEnglish: Depend entirely on one thing.
japanese: ただ一点に、すべてがかかっている。
cue: One approval decides a whole project. Say so.
reply: The whole plan hinges on the permit.
transferCue: Describe a decision that depends on one number.
transferReply: It hinges on whether the rent goes up.
nuance: Inseparable. Stronger than depend on: it names a single decisive factor.
contrast: Hinge on names one decisive factor; depend on allows several.

meaning: Separate part of an organisation and make it independent.
easyEnglish: Separate part of an organisation and make it independent.
japanese: 一部門を切り離して、独立させる。
cue: A division became its own company. Report it.
reply: They hived off the research arm last year.
transferCue: Describe a proposal for a service.
transferReply: The plan is to hive off maintenance into a separate team.
nuance: Separable: hive it off. British and mostly used about businesses and departments.
contrast: Hive off separates a unit; spin off usually creates a new company from it.

meaning: Refuse to accept less than what you want.
easyEnglish: Refuse to accept less than what you want.
japanese: 望む条件が出るまで、引き下がらない。
cue: An offer is below your minimum. State your position.
reply: I'd hold out for the full amount.
transferCue: Describe waiting for the right flat.
transferReply: They held out for a garden and waited eight months.
nuance: Inseparable; for introduces what you insist on. It implies patience as well as refusal.
contrast: Hold out for waits for better terms; stand your ground refuses to move at all.

meaning: Force someone to leave through constant pressure.
easyEnglish: Force someone to leave through constant pressure.
japanese: 執拗な圧力で、辞めさせる。
cue: A public figure resigned after sustained criticism. Describe it.
reply: He was hounded out of the job within a month.
transferCue: Describe why someone left a club.
transferReply: She felt hounded out rather than asked to go.
nuance: Separable and usually passive: be hounded out. Of introduces the job or place.
contrast: Hound out forces someone out by pressure; freeze out excludes them quietly.

meaning: Settle in and prepare to wait out something difficult.
easyEnglish: Settle in and prepare to wait out something difficult.
japanese: 腰を据えて、じっと持ちこたえる。
cue: A difficult quarter is ahead. Describe the approach.
reply: We'll hunker down and get through the winter.
transferCue: Describe a household before a storm.
transferReply: We hunkered down with candles and waited.
nuance: Intransitive and informal. It implies staying put rather than acting.
contrast: Hunker down waits something out; ride out survives it without the sense of hiding.

meaning: Search until you find someone or something.
easyEnglish: Search until you find someone or something.
japanese: 見つかるまで、徹底的に探す。
cue: A missing document turned up after a long search.
reply: I hunted down the original contract in the archive.
transferCue: Describe finding a rare item.
transferReply: She hunted down a replacement part online.
nuance: Separable: hunt it down. It implies persistence, not a quick look.
contrast: Hunt down finds after searching; track down is a close alternative.

meaning: Stop information from becoming public.
easyEnglish: Stop information from becoming public.
japanese: 表沙汰にならないよう、もみ消す。
cue: An incident was never reported. Describe the claim.
reply: The report says the whole thing was hushed up.
transferCue: Argue for openness.
transferReply: Trying to hush it up would make it worse.
nuance: Separable: hush it up. Always disapproving, and often passive.
contrast: Hush up suppresses information; gloss over mentions it but minimises it.

meaning: Make something more interesting or attractive.
easyEnglish: Make something more interesting or attractive.
japanese: 手を加えて、見栄えや面白みを足す。
cue: A plain room needs improving cheaply. Suggest something.
reply: We could jazz it up with a rug and a lamp.
transferCue: Describe improving a simple dish.
transferReply: A bit of lemon jazzes up the whole thing.
nuance: Separable: jazz it up. Informal, and about surface appeal rather than substance.
contrast: Jazz up adds appeal; spruce up makes something tidy and fresh.

meaning: Become a member, or connect separate parts.
easyEnglish: Become a member, or connect separate parts.
japanese: 入会する。ばらばらのものをつなぐ。
cue: A friend is considering a local club.
reply: You should join up — the first month is free.
transferCue: Describe connecting two paths.
transferReply: The two routes join up beyond the bridge.
nuance: Intransitive for membership; join something up connects parts. Joined-up thinking means well connected.
contrast: Join up becomes a member; join in takes part in an activity already happening.

meaning: Fall over suddenly.
easyEnglish: Fall over suddenly.
japanese: ばったりと倒れる。
cue: Describe someone fainting in the heat.
reply: He nearly keeled over in the queue.
transferCue: Describe a tree after a storm.
transferReply: The old pine keeled over in the night.
nuance: Intransitive and informal. It suggests a sudden fall, often from illness or wind.
contrast: Keel over falls suddenly; pass out is losing consciousness.

meaning: Type information into a system.
easyEnglish: Type information into a system.
japanese: データを入力する。
cue: Explain a step in a process.
reply: Key in the reference before you press submit.
transferCue: Describe a data-entry job.
transferReply: She keyed in four hundred records in a day.
nuance: Separable: key it in. Slightly dated; type in or enter is more common now.
contrast: Key in types data; log in identifies you to a system.

meaning: Discuss an idea informally.
easyEnglish: Discuss an idea informally.
japanese: 案を気楽に出し合って検討する。
cue: A team needs early ideas, not decisions.
reply: Let's kick a few ideas around before Friday.
transferCue: Describe an informal planning session.
transferReply: We kicked the proposal around over lunch.
nuance: Separable: kick it around. Informal, and it implies no commitment yet.
contrast: Kick around explores ideas loosely; thrash out reaches an agreement.

meaning: Stop work for the day, or reduce a price.
easyEnglish: Stop work for the day, or reduce a price.
japanese: 仕事を切り上げる。値引きする。
cue: It is late and the work can wait. Suggest stopping.
reply: Shall we knock off and finish in the morning?
transferCue: Describe a discount at a market.
transferReply: He knocked off ten pounds for cash.
nuance: Intransitive for finishing work; separable for a price: knock it off. Knock it off! also means stop that.
contrast: Knock off ends the working day; clock off records that you have left.

meaning: Fasten shoes or boots with laces.
easyEnglish: Fasten shoes or boots with laces.
japanese: 靴ひもを結ぶ。
cue: You are getting ready for a walk.
reply: Give me a second to lace up my boots.
transferCue: Describe a runner before a race.
transferReply: She laced up her shoes and went to the line.
nuance: Separable: lace them up. The adjective is lace-up, as in lace-up boots.
contrast: Lace up fastens laces; do up fastens any kind of clothing.

meaning: End up somewhere or in some state, unintentionally.
easyEnglish: End up somewhere or in some state, unintentionally.
japanese: 思いがけず、ある場所や状態に行き着く。
cue: A journey went wrong. Describe where you ended.
reply: We landed up in a town nobody had heard of.
transferCue: Describe an unplanned career.
transferReply: He landed up teaching, which he never planned.
nuance: Intransitive and British; American English says end up. It implies the result was not planned.
contrast: Land up is an unplanned outcome; settle down is choosing to stay somewhere.

meaning: Treat something as unimportant by joking about it.
easyEnglish: Treat something as unimportant by joking about it.
japanese: 冗談にして、軽く受け流す。
cue: Someone made light of a minor injury. Describe it.
reply: She laughed it off and carried on playing.
transferCue: Advise against dismissing a concern.
transferReply: I wouldn't laugh off a warning like that.
nuance: Separable: laugh it off. It can show resilience or unwise dismissal, depending on what is dismissed.
contrast: Laugh off dismisses with humour; shrug off dismisses without reacting at all.

meaning: Start doing or saying something with energy, often at length.
easyEnglish: Start doing or saying something with energy, often at length.
japanese: 勢いよく、長々と始める。
cue: A colleague started a long explanation unprompted. Describe it.
reply: He launched into the history of the project.
transferCue: Describe starting a piece of music.
transferReply: The band launched into the final song.
nuance: Inseparable. It suggests suddenness and length, so it is often mildly critical of a speech.
contrast: Launch into starts energetically; dive into stresses eagerness rather than length.

meaning: Criticise or attack someone strongly.
easyEnglish: Criticise or attack someone strongly.
japanese: 激しく非難する。
cue: A review meeting became harsh. Describe it.
reply: The client laid into us about the delay.
transferCue: Describe a critical newspaper column.
transferReply: The piece lays into the whole policy.
nuance: Inseparable and informal. Lay is irregular: laid. Strong, so keep it for real criticism.
contrast: Lay into attacks verbally at length; tell off is a shorter reprimand.

meaning: Encourage someone to believe something that is not true.
easyEnglish: Encourage someone to believe something that is not true.
japanese: 期待を持たせて、思わせぶりにする。
cue: A supplier implied a discount that never existed. Describe it.
reply: They led us on about the price for weeks.
transferCue: Warn against giving false hope.
transferReply: Don't lead him on if you've already decided.
nuance: Separable: lead them on. Lead is irregular: led. Always disapproving.
contrast: Lead on creates false hope; put off discourages someone instead.

meaning: Turn the pages of something quickly.
easyEnglish: Turn the pages of something quickly.
japanese: ページをぱらぱらとめくって見る。
cue: You looked at a book without reading it properly.
reply: I leafed through it in the shop and put it back.
transferCue: Describe waiting in a reception area.
transferReply: He leafed through a magazine for ten minutes.
nuance: Inseparable. Only for things with pages, and it implies no real reading.
contrast: Leaf through skims pages; pore over studies them closely.

meaning: Accept an opportunity eagerly and at once.
easyEnglish: Accept an opportunity eagerly and at once.
japanese: 好機に、すぐ飛びつく。
cue: A colleague was offered a secondment. Describe the response.
reply: She leapt at the chance to work abroad.
transferCue: Describe your own reaction to an offer.
transferReply: I'd leap at an offer like that.
nuance: Inseparable. Both leapt and leaped are used. Almost always with chance, opportunity or offer.
contrast: Leap at accepts eagerly; jump on can mean seizing on someone's mistake.

meaning: Become less strong, or stop for a while.
easyEnglish: Become less strong, or stop for a while.
japanese: 勢いが弱まる。一時的にやむ。
cue: Heavy rain has continued all day. Comment.
reply: If the rain lets up we could still go.
transferCue: Describe a demanding period at work.
transferReply: The pressure hasn't let up since January.
nuance: Intransitive. Used for weather, pressure and effort, and often in the negative.
contrast: Let up is something easing on its own; ease up is a person doing less.

meaning: Stop rising or falling and stay steady.
easyEnglish: Stop rising or falling and stay steady.
japanese: 変動が止まり、安定する。
cue: A rising cost has stabilised. Report it.
reply: Prices levelled off in the second half.
transferCue: Describe a plane after take-off.
transferReply: The plane levelled off at thirty thousand feet.
nuance: Intransitive. British doubles the l: levelled. Level out is an equally common variant.
contrast: Level off stops changing; fall back means returning to a lower level.

meaning: Stay in bed later than usual.
easyEnglish: Stay in bed later than usual.
japanese: いつもより遅くまで寝ている。
cue: A friend asks about your Sunday.
reply: I lie in on Sundays and make a proper breakfast.
transferCue: Describe a rare morning off.
transferReply: We lay in until ten for the first time in months.
nuance: Intransitive and British; the noun is a lie-in. Lie is irregular: lay, lain.
contrast: Lie in stays in bed by choice; sleep in can also mean oversleeping.

meaning: Do gentle exercises to prepare your body.
easyEnglish: Do gentle exercises to prepare your body.
japanese: 軽く体をほぐして、準備する。
cue: You are about to start a run with a friend.
reply: Let's limber up before we start.
transferCue: Describe a musician before a concert.
transferReply: She limbers up her hands before every performance.
nuance: Intransitive. About loosening muscles specifically, not general preparation.
contrast: Limber up loosens the body; warm up can also mean preparing an audience or a machine.

meaning: Join with someone or something to work together.
easyEnglish: Join with someone or something to work together.
japanese: 連携して、つながる。
cue: Two teams will collaborate next month. Describe it.
reply: We link up with the Osaka office in October.
transferCue: Describe meeting someone during a journey.
transferReply: We'll link up with them at the station.
nuance: Intransitive with with, or link something up. The noun is a link-up.
contrast: Link up joins forces; team up stresses working as one group.

meaning: Listen to a conversation you are not part of.
easyEnglish: Listen to a conversation you are not part of.
japanese: 自分が当事者でない会話を、そばで聞く。
cue: You want to observe a call without speaking.
reply: Can I listen in on the handover call?
transferCue: Describe overhearing a discussion.
transferReply: I listened in for a minute and left.
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces the conversation. Asking permission makes it polite rather than intrusive.
contrast: Listen in joins as an observer; eavesdrop is always secret.

meaning: Make something more lively, or become more lively.
easyEnglish: Make something more lively, or become more lively.
japanese: 活気づける。活気づく。
cue: A quiet gathering improved after music started.
reply: The evening livened up once the music started.
transferCue: Suggest improving a dull presentation.
transferReply: A short video would liven it up.
nuance: Separable: liven it up, or intransitive. About atmosphere and energy.
contrast: Liven up adds energy; jazz up adds visual or surface appeal.

meaning: Put something in a locked place for safety.
easyEnglish: Put something in a locked place for safety.
japanese: 鍵をかけて、しまい込む。
cue: Valuables need storing during building work.
reply: We locked away the documents until the work finished.
transferCue: Describe keeping medicine safe.
transferReply: Lock it away where the children can't reach.
nuance: Separable: lock it away. Also used figuratively about keeping feelings hidden.
contrast: Lock away stores securely; lock out leaves someone unable to get in.

meaning: Watch something without taking part.
easyEnglish: Watch something without taking part.
japanese: 加わらずに、そばで見ている。
cue: Describe bystanders at an incident.
reply: A crowd looked on while the staff cleared the road.
transferCue: Describe a coach during a match.
transferReply: He looked on from the side without shouting.
nuance: Intransitive. It implies not intervening, which can sound passive.
contrast: Look on watches without acting; look after takes responsibility for someone.

meaning: Manage to succeed despite having no clear plan.
easyEnglish: Manage to succeed despite having no clear plan.
japanese: 手探りでも、なんとか切り抜ける。
cue: A task was done without proper instructions. Describe it.
reply: We had no manual, so we muddled through.
transferCue: Describe a first attempt at cooking something.
transferReply: I muddled through and it tasted fine.
nuance: Intransitive and British. Modest rather than proud: it admits the process was messy.
contrast: Muddle through succeeds without a plan; make do manages with limited resources.

meaning: Eat something in small bites, or show slight interest.
easyEnglish: Eat something in small bites, or show slight interest.
japanese: 少しずつかじる。わずかに関心を示す。
cue: Someone is not eating much at dinner. Describe it.
reply: She nibbled at the bread and left the rest.
transferCue: Describe a buyer's early interest.
transferReply: Two buyers are nibbling at the offer.
nuance: Inseparable. Literal for food, figurative for tentative interest or slow reduction.
contrast: Nibble at takes small bites; wolf down eats very quickly.

meaning: Achieve a number of wins or results.
easyEnglish: Achieve a number of wins or results.
japanese: 勝利や実績を、積み上げる。
cue: A team has reached a milestone. Report it.
reply: They notched up their hundredth sale this week.
transferCue: Describe a long-running show.
transferReply: The play has notched up five hundred performances.
nuance: Separable: notch them up. Used with countable achievements such as wins or sales.
contrast: Notch up counts achievements; chalk up can also record a loss as experience.

meaning: Stop doing something, or attract a large number of people.
easyEnglish: Stop doing something, or attract a large number of people.
japanese: やめる。また、大勢を呼び込む。
cue: A friend is considering leaving a long-held job.
reply: He's thinking of packing in the commute and working locally.
transferCue: Describe a popular venue.
transferReply: That little theatre packs in three hundred a night.
nuance: Separable: pack it in. British and informal. Pack it in! also means stop that.
contrast: Pack in quits something; pack up can mean finishing for the day or breaking down.

meaning: Reduce something to what is essential.
easyEnglish: Reduce something to what is essential.
japanese: 必要な分だけに、削り込む。
cue: A document is too long for its audience.
reply: Let's pare it down to two pages.
transferCue: Describe simplifying a household.
transferReply: We pared down our things before the move.
nuance: Separable: pare it down. To introduces what remains. Slightly formal.
contrast: Pare down removes the inessential; cut back reduces an amount or an activity.

meaning: Blame someone for something, often unfairly.
easyEnglish: Blame someone for something, often unfairly.
japanese: 責任を、その人になすりつける。
cue: One person was blamed for a shared failure. Describe it.
reply: They pinned the whole delay on the newest member.
transferCue: Refuse to accept misplaced blame.
transferReply: Don't pin that on me — I raised it in March.
nuance: The thing blamed goes between pin and on. It usually implies the blame is unfair.
contrast: Pin on assigns blame to a person; put down to explains a cause without blame.

meaning: Suddenly speak, often after being silent.
easyEnglish: Suddenly speak, often after being silent.
japanese: 黙っていた人が、ふいに口を開く。
cue: A quiet person made the key point. Describe it.
reply: Then Ken piped up with the obvious answer.
transferCue: Describe a child joining an adult conversation.
transferReply: She piped up from the back seat.
nuance: Intransitive; with introduces what was said. Informal and slightly affectionate.
contrast: Pipe up breaks a silence; speak up means saying it louder or more assertively.

meaning: Join in and help with a shared task.
easyEnglish: Join in and help with a shared task.
japanese: みんなの作業に加わって、手伝う。
cue: A group is clearing up after an event.
reply: If everyone pitches in we'll be done by six.
transferCue: Thank neighbours after a working day.
transferReply: Four neighbours pitched in and it took half the time.
nuance: Intransitive; with introduces the task. Warm and informal, about shared effort.
contrast: Pitch in joins a shared effort; help out can be helping one person.

meaning: Keep working steadily at something difficult.
easyEnglish: Keep working steadily at something difficult.
japanese: 地道に、こつこつ続ける。
cue: Progress is slow but continuing. Describe it.
reply: We're plugging away at the backlog.
transferCue: Describe learning an instrument.
transferReply: I plug away at it for twenty minutes a day.
nuance: Intransitive; at introduces the task. It accepts slow progress without complaint.
contrast: Plug away continues steadily; press on stresses continuing despite obstacles.

meaning: Choose one option after hesitating.
easyEnglish: Choose one option after hesitating.
japanese: 迷った末に、ひとつに決める。
cue: You could not decide between two dishes.
reply: In the end I plumped for the fish.
transferCue: Describe choosing a colour.
transferReply: We plumped for the darker green.
nuance: Inseparable, informal and British. It implies hesitation before the choice.
contrast: Plump for chooses after hesitating; settle on suggests the search is finally over.

meaning: Improve something that is already reasonably good.
easyEnglish: Improve something that is already reasonably good.
japanese: ある程度できているものを、さらに磨く。
cue: A draft is nearly ready but needs care.
reply: I'll polish up the wording before it goes out.
transferCue: Describe preparing a language skill.
transferReply: She polished up her French before the trip.
nuance: Separable: polish it up. It assumes a working version already exists.
contrast: Polish up refines what exists; flesh out adds missing substance.

meaning: Seize on something eagerly, especially a mistake.
easyEnglish: Seize on something eagerly, especially a mistake.
japanese: すかさず飛びつく。あらを見つけて突く。
cue: A small error drew immediate criticism. Describe it.
reply: The press pounced on the one wrong figure.
transferCue: Describe a buyer reacting to a listing.
transferReply: Someone pounced on it within an hour.
nuance: Inseparable. It suggests speed and eagerness, often to criticise.
contrast: Pounce on seizes eagerly; jump at is about accepting an opportunity.

meaning: Demand something repeatedly and firmly.
easyEnglish: Demand something repeatedly and firmly.
japanese: 繰り返し強く求める。
cue: A group wants a clear answer from management. Describe it.
reply: The union is pressing for a written commitment.
transferCue: Describe asking for a refund.
transferReply: I pressed for a full refund and got one.
nuance: Inseparable; for introduces the demand. Firmer than ask for, without being rude.
contrast: Press for demands persistently; push for stresses driving something forward.

meaning: Support something that would otherwise fail or fall.
easyEnglish: Support something that would otherwise fail or fall.
japanese: 倒れないように、下支えする。
cue: One product funds a struggling business. Describe it.
reply: Exports have propped up the company for years.
transferCue: Describe a fence after a storm.
transferReply: We propped up the fence with two posts.
nuance: Separable: prop it up. Often mildly critical when it means keeping something alive artificially.
contrast: Prop up keeps something from failing; back up supports a claim with evidence.

meaning: Work something out by thinking hard.
easyEnglish: Work something out by thinking hard.
japanese: 頭をひねって、解き明かす。
cue: An unclear instruction eventually made sense.
reply: It took an hour to puzzle out what they meant.
transferCue: Describe reading an old handwritten letter.
transferReply: We puzzled out most of the words together.
nuance: Separable: puzzle it out. It emphasises effort on something deliberately unclear.
contrast: Puzzle out decodes something obscure; figure out is the everyday equivalent.

meaning: Have discovered something important, or suspect what someone is doing.
easyEnglish: Have discovered something important, or suspect what someone is doing.
japanese: 重要なことに気づいている。相手の企みを察している。
cue: A colleague's early theory turned out right. Tell them.
reply: I think you are onto something with that pattern.
transferCue: Describe someone who realised what was happening.
transferReply: The auditors were onto them within a week.
nuance: Inseparable and always with be. Onto something is positive discovery; onto someone is suspicion.
contrast: Be onto has discovered something; be into means being interested in it.

meaning: Fill an opening so nothing can pass through.
easyEnglish: Fill an opening so nothing can pass through.
japanese: ふさいで、通れなくする。
cue: A sink is draining slowly. Describe the cause.
reply: Something is blocking up the pipe.
transferCue: Describe a blocked nose during a cold.
transferReply: My nose has been blocked up since Tuesday.
nuance: Separable: block it up. Often passive about noses and pipes.
contrast: Block up fills an opening; block off closes a route or reserves time.

meaning: Practise something you once knew to make it good again.
easyEnglish: Practise something you once knew to make it good again.
japanese: 以前できたことを、練習して取り戻す。
cue: You will need a language you have not used for years.
reply: I should brush up my Spanish before the trip.
transferCue: Describe preparing for an interview.
transferReply: She brushed up on the company's recent work.
nuance: Separable, with or without on. It assumes you knew the thing before.
contrast: Brush up refreshes old knowledge; mug up learns something quickly for a test.

meaning: Take strict action to stop something.
easyEnglish: Take strict action to stop something.
japanese: 厳しく取り締まる。
cue: A policy on expenses has tightened. Describe it.
reply: Finance is clamping down on late claims.
transferCue: Describe enforcement in a neighbourhood.
transferReply: The council clamped down on pavement parking.
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces what is being stopped. The noun is a clampdown.
contrast: Clamp down enforces strictly; crack down is an equally common alternative.

meaning: Record that you are finishing work.
easyEnglish: Record that you are finishing work.
japanese: 退勤の打刻をする。仕事を終える。
cue: A shift is ending. Tell a colleague your plan.
reply: I clock off at six and I'm not coming back.
transferCue: Describe a workplace routine.
transferReply: Everyone clocks off at the same time on Fridays.
nuance: Intransitive. British says clock off, American clock out. Clock on is the opposite.
contrast: Clock off records leaving; knock off simply means stopping work.

meaning: Regain consciousness, or visit someone's home.
easyEnglish: Regain consciousness, or visit someone's home.
japanese: 意識を取り戻す。家に立ち寄る。
cue: Invite a friend to your home at the weekend.
reply: Come round on Sunday and we'll cook something.
transferCue: Describe someone waking after fainting.
transferReply: He came round after a minute and sat up.
nuance: Intransitive and British; American English says come around. A third sense is changing your opinion.
contrast: Come round visits or revives; bring round persuades someone to agree.

meaning: Start dealing much more strictly with a problem.
easyEnglish: Start dealing much more strictly with a problem.
japanese: 問題に対して、急に厳しく対処し始める。
cue: Enforcement of a rule has suddenly increased.
reply: They've started cracking down on unlicensed stalls.
transferCue: Describe a school's new approach.
transferReply: The school cracked down on phones in class.
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces the target. The noun is a crackdown, written as one word.
contrast: Crack down starts strict enforcement; clamp down stresses keeping it suppressed.

meaning: Give something to each person in turn.
easyEnglish: Give something to each person in turn.
japanese: 一人ずつに、順に配る。
cue: You are starting a card game.
reply: Deal out five cards each and we'll begin.
transferCue: Describe distributing tasks unevenly.
transferReply: The work was dealt out unequally.
nuance: Separable: deal them out. From card games, and also used for punishment or justice.
contrast: Deal out distributes in turn; divvy up splits into shares.

meaning: Confront an opponent directly.
easyEnglish: Confront an opponent directly.
japanese: 相手と正面から向き合う。
cue: Two candidates will debate publicly. Describe it.
reply: The two of them face off on Thursday evening.
transferCue: Describe two teams meeting again.
transferReply: They faced off in the final for the third year.
nuance: Intransitive; against introduces the opponent. The noun is a face-off, written with a hyphen.
contrast: Face off is a direct confrontation; face up to is accepting a difficult fact.

meaning: Look after yourself without help.
easyEnglish: Look after yourself without help.
japanese: 人に頼らず、自分の面倒を見る。
cue: You will be away and your teenager is at home.
reply: He can fend for himself for two nights.
transferCue: Describe a cat left with a neighbour.
transferReply: She's not used to fending for herself.
nuance: The reflexive follows the subject and is required: fend for yourself, not fend for.
contrast: Fend for yourself manages alone; stand on your own two feet is about lasting independence.

meaning: Complete the last part of something.
easyEnglish: Complete the last part of something.
japanese: 最後の部分を仕上げる。
cue: Most of a task is done and a little remains.
reply: I'll finish up the notes and send them tonight.
transferCue: Describe the end of a meal.
transferReply: Finish up your soup and we'll go.
nuance: Separable: finish it up. British also uses finish up meaning end somewhere unexpectedly.
contrast: Finish up completes the remainder; finish off can also mean using the last of something.

meaning: Work well alongside something else.
easyEnglish: Work well alongside something else.
japanese: ほかのものと、うまく噛み合う。
cue: A proposed date must work with existing plans.
reply: Does Tuesday fit in with your schedule?
transferCue: Describe a new piece of furniture.
transferReply: The table fits in with the rest of the room.
nuance: Inseparable. With introduces what it must match — a plan, a style or a group.
contrast: Fit in with matches an existing thing; fit in is about belonging in a group.

meaning: Remove clothing quickly and carelessly.
easyEnglish: Remove clothing quickly and carelessly.
japanese: 衣類を、勢いよく脱ぎ捨てる。
cue: Describe coming home on a hot day.
reply: I flung off my coat and opened every window.
transferCue: Describe a child after school.
transferReply: She flings off her shoes the moment she's inside.
nuance: Separable: fling it off. Fling is irregular: flung. It implies speed and carelessness.
contrast: Fling off removes clothing quickly; take off is the neutral verb.

meaning: Bend something so it becomes smaller and flatter.
easyEnglish: Bend something so it becomes smaller and flatter.
japanese: 折りたたんで、小さくする。
cue: You are tidying after a picnic.
reply: Could you fold up the blanket while I pack?
transferCue: Describe a compact chair.
transferReply: The chairs fold up and slide under the bed.
nuance: Separable: fold it up. The adjective is fold-up, as in a fold-up chair.
contrast: Fold up makes something compact; pack up puts things away to leave.

meaning: Happen or come after something else.
easyEnglish: Happen or come after something else.
japanese: 前のものに続いて起こる。
cue: Explain how two sessions relate.
reply: The workshop follows on from this morning's talk.
transferCue: Describe a second email.
transferReply: This follows on from my message yesterday.
nuance: Intransitive; from introduces what came before. Common in writing to link two items.
contrast: Follow on continues from something; follow up returns to it with further action.

meaning: Become friendly with someone, often for an advantage.
easyEnglish: Become friendly with someone, often for an advantage.
japanese: 取り入って、親しくなる。
cue: Someone is cultivating a useful contact. Describe it.
reply: He's trying to get in with the organisers.
transferCue: Describe a newcomer finding a group.
transferReply: She got in with the cycling crowd quickly.
nuance: Inseparable. It can be neutral about making friends, or critical about seeking advantage.
contrast: Get in with joins a circle; suck up to is openly flattering someone.

meaning: Stop doing something annoying.
easyEnglish: Stop doing something annoying.
japanese: いいかげんに、やめる。
cue: Someone keeps teasing you about the same thing.
reply: Give over — you've said that three times.
transferCue: Describe telling children to settle.
transferReply: They gave over as soon as the food arrived.
nuance: Intransitive, informal and northern British. As a command it is blunt but usually good-humoured.
contrast: Give over tells someone to stop; give up means abandoning an attempt.

meaning: Keep something rather than giving it away.
easyEnglish: Keep something rather than giving it away.
japanese: 手放さずに、持っておく。
cue: A friend is clearing out old paperwork. Advise caution.
reply: Hang onto the receipts for another year.
transferCue: Describe keeping an old device.
transferReply: I hung onto the old phone as a spare.
nuance: Inseparable. Written as one word or two. Hang is irregular: hung.
contrast: Hang onto keeps a thing; hang on means waiting a moment.

meaning: Give someone a great deal of praise or blame at once.
easyEnglish: Give someone a great deal of praise or blame at once.
japanese: 称賛や非難を、どっと浴びせる。
cue: A colleague received extravagant praise. Describe it.
reply: The director heaped praise on the whole team.
transferCue: Describe unfair criticism.
transferReply: They heaped the blame on one person.
nuance: The praise or blame goes between heap and on. It stresses quantity, which can sound excessive.
contrast: Heap on pours praise or blame; pin on assigns blame to one person.

meaning: Connect something to a larger system.
easyEnglish: Connect something to a larger system.
japanese: 大きな仕組みに、つなぎ込む。
cue: Explain how a new tool will work with existing ones.
reply: It hooks into the booking system directly.
transferCue: Describe connecting a device.
transferReply: We hooked the speaker into the main amplifier.
nuance: Separable: hook it into. Technical, about connections rather than relationships.
contrast: Hook into connects to a system; hook up can also mean meeting someone.

meaning: Investigate something officially.
easyEnglish: Investigate something officially.
japanese: 公式に調査する。
cue: A formal review has been opened. Report it.
reply: A panel will inquire into how the decision was made.
transferCue: Describe a historical investigation.
transferReply: The commission inquired into the causes for two years.
nuance: Inseparable and formal. British also spells it enquire; American prefers inquire.
contrast: Inquire into is a formal investigation; look into is the everyday equivalent.

meaning: Compete with others for an advantage.
easyEnglish: Compete with others for an advantage.
japanese: 有利な位置を求めて、competing する相手と張り合う。
cue: Several people want the same opportunity. Describe it.
reply: Three of them are jockeying for the same role.
transferCue: Describe drivers before a start.
transferReply: The cars jockeyed for position on the first lap.
nuance: Inseparable, usually in the continuous and very often with position. Mildly critical of the manoeuvring.
contrast: Jockey for manoeuvres for advantage; compete with names the rival directly.

meaning: Join a conversation or activity suddenly.
easyEnglish: Join a conversation or activity suddenly.
japanese: 会話や作業に、途中から入る。
cue: You want to add something during a discussion.
reply: Can I jump in here for a second?
transferCue: Invite someone to contribute.
transferReply: Jump in any time if I've got this wrong.
nuance: Intransitive and informal. Asking first makes it polite rather than an interruption.
contrast: Jump in joins a discussion; butt in interrupts without invitation.

meaning: Reject a proposal, or drink something quickly.
easyEnglish: Reject a proposal, or drink something quickly.
japanese: 提案を突き返す。一気に飲む。
cue: A planning application was refused. Report it.
reply: The council knocked back the application twice.
transferCue: Describe someone finishing a drink fast.
transferReply: He knocked back his coffee and left.
nuance: Separable: knock it back. British and informal, with two distinct senses that context separates.
contrast: Knock back rejects bluntly; turn down is the neutral word.

meaning: Make something quickly from what is available.
easyEnglish: Make something quickly from what is available.
japanese: ありあわせで、手早く作る。
cue: Guests arrived unexpectedly at dinner time.
reply: I'll knock together something with what's in the fridge.
transferCue: Describe building a temporary shelf.
transferReply: He knocked together a shelf from old boards.
nuance: Separable: knock it together. Informal and British, and it accepts rough quality.
contrast: Knock together builds quickly; throw together stresses that ingredients were whatever was there.

meaning: Continue to exist or endure until the end of a period.
easyEnglish: Continue to exist or endure until the end of a period.
japanese: 最後まで、もちこたえる。
cue: Supplies may not cover the whole week.
reply: I don't think the paper will last out the month.
transferCue: Describe someone enduring a difficult job.
transferReply: She lasted out the full contract and then left.
nuance: Inseparable. British, and it implies difficulty in continuing to the end.
contrast: Last out endures to the end; hold out for waits for better terms.

meaning: Provide something for a group, often free.
easyEnglish: Provide something for a group, often free.
japanese: 一同のために、用意して提供する。
cue: An event will include refreshments. Announce it.
reply: The company is laying on lunch for everyone.
transferCue: Describe transport at a wedding.
transferReply: They laid on a bus from the station.
nuance: Separable: lay it on. Lay is irregular: laid. British, about hospitality or services provided.
contrast: Lay on provides for a group; put on can also mean staging a performance.

meaning: Cause something to happen later.
easyEnglish: Cause something to happen later.
japanese: 結果として、あることを引き起こす。
cue: One decision produced a series of effects.
reply: The delay led to three other problems.
transferCue: Describe how a hobby became a job.
transferReply: A weekend class led to a career change.
nuance: Inseparable. Lead is irregular: led. The cause is the subject, and the result follows to.
contrast: Lead to names a consequence; result in is a more formal equivalent.

meaning: Become known when it was meant to be secret.
easyEnglish: Become known when it was meant to be secret.
japanese: 秘密が、外に漏れる。
cue: News spread before the official announcement.
reply: The date leaked out before we could tell the team.
transferCue: Describe a confidential document.
transferReply: Details leaked out within hours.
nuance: Intransitive; the information is the subject. Leak something is transitive and means releasing it deliberately.
contrast: Leak out escapes accidentally; give away reveals something by mistake in speech.

meaning: Become bright, or show sudden happiness.
easyEnglish: Become bright, or show sudden happiness.
japanese: 明るくなる。ぱっと顔がほころぶ。
cue: Describe a child seeing a surprise.
reply: Her face lit up when she saw the cake.
transferCue: Describe a building in the evening.
transferReply: The bridge lights up at half past six.
nuance: Intransitive here. Light is irregular: lit. Light something up is transitive.
contrast: Light up shows sudden delight; brighten up is a gradual improvement in mood or weather.

meaning: Consider something the most important part of your life.
easyEnglish: Consider something the most important part of your life.
japanese: それを生きがいにしている。
cue: A colleague's weekends are entirely about music.
reply: He lives for Saturday nights at the club.
transferCue: Describe a devoted coach.
transferReply: She lives for the team and always has.
nuance: Inseparable. It describes devotion, so it sounds strong; live off means depending on for income.
contrast: Live for is what gives life meaning; live off is what pays for it.

meaning: Become less tense or less strict.
easyEnglish: Become less tense or less strict.
japanese: 緊張や堅苦しさが、ほぐれる。
cue: A nervous group relaxed after an introduction game.
reply: Everyone loosened up after the first exercise.
transferCue: Describe a rule becoming less strict.
transferReply: The dress code has loosened up a lot.
nuance: Intransitive, or loosen something up. About tension in people and strictness in rules.
contrast: Loosen up reduces tension; limber up is specifically preparing muscles.

meaning: Be unexpectedly lucky.
easyEnglish: Be unexpectedly lucky.
japanese: 思いがけず、運に恵まれる。
cue: You got the last seat on a full train.
reply: I lucked out and got the last seat.
transferCue: Describe finding a flat quickly.
transferReply: We lucked out with the second place we viewed.
nuance: Intransitive, informal and American. Note that it means being lucky, not running out of luck.
contrast: Luck out is unexpected good fortune; hit the jackpot stresses the size of the win.

meaning: Treat different things as if they were the same.
easyEnglish: Treat different things as if they were the same.
japanese: 違うものを、ひとまとめに扱う。
cue: A report treats two very different groups identically. Object.
reply: The figures lump together students and staff.
transferCue: Ask for a distinction.
transferReply: Please don't lump the two regions together.
nuance: Separable: lump them together. Usually critical of a distinction being lost.
contrast: Lump together merges categories; tell apart distinguishes them.

meaning: Reach the highest possible limit.
easyEnglish: Reach the highest possible limit.
japanese: 上限まで使い切る。限界に達する。
cue: A storage allowance is full. Report it.
reply: We've maxed out the shared drive again.
transferCue: Describe reaching a physical limit.
transferReply: He maxed out at eighty kilos.
nuance: Separable: max it out. Informal and American in origin, now common in both.
contrast: Max out reaches a ceiling; use up finishes a supply.

meaning: Be good enough compared with a standard.
easyEnglish: Be good enough compared with a standard.
japanese: 求められる水準に達している。
cue: A trial product did not meet expectations.
reply: The samples didn't measure up to the originals.
transferCue: Reassure someone comparing themselves to others.
transferReply: You measure up perfectly well — stop comparing.
nuance: Intransitive; to introduces the standard. Often in the negative.
contrast: Measure up meets a standard; live up to meets an expectation or a promise.

meaning: Move about in a group without clear purpose.
easyEnglish: Move about in a group without clear purpose.
japanese: 目的もなく、集まってうろうろする。
cue: A crowd waited outside before a venue opened.
reply: People milled around outside until seven.
transferCue: Describe a break at a conference.
transferReply: Everyone milled around the coffee table.
nuance: Intransitive and only about groups. British also says mill about.
contrast: Mill around is aimless group movement; hang around is waiting in one place.

meaning: Complain about something repeatedly.
easyEnglish: Complain about something repeatedly.
japanese: 繰り返し、ぶつぶつ不満を言う。
cue: A colleague complains about the same thing daily.
reply: He moans about the coffee every single morning.
transferCue: Admit to complaining yourself.
transferReply: I shouldn't moan about the weather so much.
nuance: Inseparable, informal and British. It implies the complaining is unproductive.
contrast: Moan about is low-level grumbling; kick up a fuss is loud and public.

meaning: Clean up liquid, or finish the last remaining tasks.
easyEnglish: Clean up liquid, or finish the last remaining tasks.
japanese: こぼれたものを拭き取る。残りを片づける。
cue: Someone spilled water on the floor.
reply: I'll mop up the spill before it spreads.
transferCue: Describe the end of a project.
transferReply: We spent Friday mopping up the last details.
nuance: Separable: mop it up. Literal for liquid, figurative for remaining work.
contrast: Mop up clears what is left; tie up loose ends finishes small outstanding tasks.

meaning: Talk loudly and rudely, often about something you know little about.
easyEnglish: Talk loudly and rudely, often about something you know little about.
japanese: 大きな口をたたく。えらそうに言い散らす。
cue: Someone criticised loudly without knowing the details.
reply: He was mouthing off about a report he hadn't read.
transferCue: Advise restraint online.
transferReply: There's no point mouthing off in the comments.
nuance: Intransitive and informal; about introduces the topic. Always disapproving.
contrast: Mouth off is rude and ignorant talk; speak out is raising a concern with purpose.

meaning: Force your way into something to get a share.
easyEnglish: Force your way into something to get a share.
japanese: 強引に割り込んで、分け前を取ろうとする。
cue: A larger company entered a market others built.
reply: They muscled in on a market we developed.
transferCue: Describe someone joining a project uninvited.
transferReply: He muscled in halfway through and took the credit.
nuance: Intransitive; on introduces what is being intruded upon. Always critical.
contrast: Muscle in forces entry; get in on the act joins something already popular.

meaning: Gather enough of a feeling to do something difficult.
easyEnglish: Gather enough of a feeling to do something difficult.
japanese: 気力を奮い起こす。
cue: You finally made a call you had been avoiding.
reply: I mustered up the courage to phone them.
transferCue: Describe starting a task when tired.
transferReply: I couldn't muster up any enthusiasm for it.
nuance: Separable: muster it up. Used with courage, energy and enthusiasm rather than objects.
contrast: Muster up gathers inner resolve; psych yourself up is preparing mentally for a moment.

meaning: Worry someone persistently in a small way.
easyEnglish: Worry someone persistently in a small way.
japanese: 小さな気がかりが、ずっとつきまとう。
cue: A small doubt will not go away. Describe it.
reply: Something about the figures nags at me.
transferCue: Describe a forgotten task.
transferReply: It nagged at her until she checked the door.
nuance: Inseparable; the worry is the subject. Nag someone is different: it means pestering them.
contrast: Nag at is small persistent doubt; gnaw at is heavier and more distressing.

meaning: Look around somewhere out of curiosity.
easyEnglish: Look around somewhere out of curiosity.
japanese: 好奇心から、あちこち覗いて回る。
cue: You arrived early and explored a building.
reply: I nosed around the old wing while I waited.
transferCue: Describe someone being too curious.
transferReply: I don't like people nosing around my desk.
nuance: Intransitive and informal. Harmless about places, intrusive about someone's belongings.
contrast: Nose around is casual curiosity; poke around is searching more actively.

meaning: Make something longer by adding unnecessary material.
easyEnglish: Make something longer by adding unnecessary material.
japanese: 中身の薄いものを、かさ増しする。
cue: A report meets a length requirement but says little.
reply: It's padded out with background nobody needs.
transferCue: Advise against filling space.
transferReply: Don't pad it out just to reach ten pages.
nuance: Separable: pad it out. Always critical of the padding.
contrast: Pad out adds filler; flesh out adds genuinely missing substance.

meaning: Persuade someone to accept something of poor value.
easyEnglish: Persuade someone to accept something of poor value.
japanese: 質の悪いものを、うまく押しつける。
cue: A seller gave a customer an inferior item. Describe it.
reply: They palmed off a returned unit as new.
transferCue: Describe avoiding an unwanted task.
transferReply: He palmed the paperwork off on the newest member.
nuance: Separable: palm it off. On introduces the person who receives it. Always disapproving.
contrast: Palm off passes on something poor; fob off dismisses a person with an excuse.

meaning: Do what someone wants even though it is not good.
easyEnglish: Do what someone wants even though it is not good.
japanese: よくないと分かっていて、相手に迎合する。
cue: A decision follows the loudest voices rather than the evidence.
reply: The policy panders to whoever complains most.
transferCue: Describe a programme chasing popularity.
transferReply: It panders to the audience instead of challenging them.
nuance: Inseparable and always critical. Distinct from cater for, which is neutral.
contrast: Pander to indulges harmfully; cater for simply meets a need.

meaning: Give something to each person in a group in turn.
easyEnglish: Give something to each person in a group in turn.
japanese: その場の全員に、順に回す。
cue: You have printed copies for a meeting.
reply: I'll pass around the handout before we start.
transferCue: Describe sharing photographs.
transferReply: She passed the album around the table.
nuance: Separable: pass it around. British also says pass round.
contrast: Pass around circulates one item; hand out gives each person their own.

meaning: Be accepted as something you are not.
easyEnglish: Be accepted as something you are not.
japanese: 本物でないのに、そう見なされる。
cue: A copy looked convincing. Comment.
reply: That print could pass for an original.
transferCue: Comment on someone's apparent age.
transferReply: He could pass for thirty.
nuance: Inseparable, usually with could or can. It implies a resemblance close enough to deceive.
contrast: Pass for is being mistaken for something; pass off is deliberately presenting it as that.

meaning: Come away from a surface in a layer.
easyEnglish: Come away from a surface in a layer.
japanese: 表面から、一枚めくれて剥がれる。
cue: Paint on a windowsill is failing. Describe it.
reply: The paint is peeling off the sill.
transferCue: Describe removing a label.
transferReply: Peel off the sticker before you wash it.
nuance: Separable when transitive, intransitive about paint or skin. Also used of a vehicle leaving a group.
contrast: Peel off comes away in a layer; wear off is an effect gradually fading.

meaning: Make something more lively or more interesting.
easyEnglish: Make something more lively or more interesting.
japanese: 元気づける。味や内容を引き立てる。
cue: A soup tastes flat. Suggest an improvement.
reply: A little chilli would pep it up.
transferCue: Describe improving a dull afternoon.
transferReply: Coffee and a walk pepped everyone up.
nuance: Separable: pep it up. Informal, for food, mood and energy alike.
contrast: Pep up adds energy or flavour; jazz up adds visual interest.

meaning: Remove or defeat things one at a time.
easyEnglish: Remove or defeat things one at a time.
japanese: ひとつずつ、順に片づける・仕留める。
cue: A long list of small tasks remains.
reply: Let's pick off the easy ones first.
transferCue: Describe a team beating rivals one by one.
transferReply: They picked off the other contenders one by one.
nuance: Separable: pick them off. It implies dealing with them individually rather than together.
contrast: Pick off handles items individually; wipe out removes everything at once.

meaning: Examine a group of things carefully to select or criticise.
easyEnglish: Examine a group of things carefully to select or criticise.
japanese: ひとつずつ吟味して、選ぶ・あら探しをする。
cue: A committee examined every line of a proposal.
reply: They picked over the budget line by line.
transferCue: Describe choosing fruit at a market.
transferReply: She picked over the apples before buying six.
nuance: Inseparable. Neutral about selecting, mildly critical about excessive scrutiny.
contrast: Pick over examines a set; pick holes in attacks an argument.

meaning: Miss someone or something very much.
easyEnglish: Miss someone or something very much.
japanese: 恋しくて、切なく思い続ける。
cue: A friend has moved abroad and misses home.
reply: She pines for the sea more than anything.
transferCue: Describe a dog when its owner is away.
transferReply: He pines for her whenever she travels.
nuance: Inseparable and slightly literary. It suggests lasting longing, not a passing wish.
contrast: Pine for is deep lasting longing; miss is the everyday word.

meaning: Decide the details of something in advance.
easyEnglish: Decide the details of something in advance.
japanese: 細部まで、前もって決めておく。
cue: A trip has many connections. Suggest preparation.
reply: Let's plan out the changes before we book.
transferCue: Describe preparing a week of meals.
transferReply: She plans out every meal on Sunday evening.
nuance: Separable: plan it out. The out adds thoroughness compared with plain plan.
contrast: Plan out works out the details; map out gives the overall shape.

meaning: Set two people against each other for your own benefit.
easyEnglish: Set two people against each other for your own benefit.
japanese: 二者を競わせて、自分が得をする。
cue: A buyer used two quotes against each other.
reply: They played the two suppliers off against each other.
transferCue: Describe a child with two parents.
transferReply: He plays one of us off against the other.
nuance: Separable, usually with against each other. Always disapproving of the manipulation.
contrast: Play off manipulates two parties; face off is a direct contest between them.

meaning: Search through things, often without permission.
easyEnglish: Search through things, often without permission.
japanese: あちこち探る。詮索する。
cue: You looked through a drawer for a charger.
reply: I poked around in the drawer and found one.
transferCue: Describe an inspector examining a property.
transferReply: The surveyor poked around the roof space.
nuance: Intransitive; in or around introduces the place. British also says poke about.
contrast: Poke around searches physically; look into investigates a question.

meaning: Visit somewhere very briefly.
easyEnglish: Visit somewhere very briefly.
japanese: ちょっとだけ立ち寄る。
cue: You will be passing a friend's shop.
reply: I'll pop in on my way home.
transferCue: Describe a short visit from a neighbour.
transferReply: She popped in to return the dish.
nuance: Intransitive and British. Very informal, and it implies only a few minutes.
contrast: Pop in is a brief visit; drop by is similar but slightly less hurried.

meaning: Switch a device on and let it start.
easyEnglish: Switch a device on and let it start.
japanese: 機器の電源を入れて、起動させる。
cue: Explain the first step of a process.
reply: Power up the machine and wait for the green light.
transferCue: Describe a slow computer.
transferReply: It takes four minutes to power up.
nuance: Separable or intransitive. Power down is the opposite.
contrast: Power up starts a device; fire up is more informal and also used for people.

meaning: Take advantage of people who are vulnerable.
easyEnglish: Take advantage of people who are vulnerable.
japanese: 弱い立場の人につけ込む。
cue: A scheme targets people in financial trouble. Criticise it.
reply: These lenders prey on people with no options.
transferCue: Describe a worry that will not leave you.
transferReply: The decision preyed on his mind for weeks.
nuance: Inseparable. Prey on someone's mind is a separate sense: to worry them continually.
contrast: Prey on exploits the vulnerable; take advantage of can be neutral about a situation.

meaning: Produce a paper copy from a computer.
easyEnglish: Produce a paper copy from a computer.
japanese: パソコンから印刷する。
cue: You need copies for a meeting.
reply: I'll print off six copies before we start.
transferCue: Describe preparing a ticket.
transferReply: Print off the confirmation and bring it with you.
nuance: Separable: print it off. British; print out is used in both varieties.
contrast: Print off produces copies; run off can mean producing many at speed.

meaning: Prepare yourself mentally for something demanding.
easyEnglish: Prepare yourself mentally for something demanding.
japanese: 気持ちを高めて、本番に備える。
cue: You are about to make a difficult call.
reply: Give me a minute to psych myself up.
transferCue: Describe an athlete before a race.
transferReply: He psychs himself up with the same song every time.
nuance: The reflexive follows the subject. Informal, and about the moments before an event.
contrast: Psych up prepares for one moment; muster up gathers resolve more generally.

meaning: Continue despite difficulty.
easyEnglish: Continue despite difficulty.
japanese: 困難でも、先へ進み続ける。
cue: A group is tired but close to the destination.
reply: Let's push on — it's twenty minutes to the top.
transferCue: Describe continuing a project after a setback.
transferReply: We pushed on and finished a week late.
nuance: Intransitive; with introduces the task. It accepts difficulty rather than denying it.
contrast: Push on continues despite difficulty; press ahead stresses moving forward with a plan.

meaning: Save money for future use.
easyEnglish: Save money for future use.
japanese: 将来のために、お金を取っておく。
cue: A friend asks how you manage irregular income.
reply: I put by a little every month for quiet periods.
transferCue: Describe saving for a purchase.
transferReply: They had put by enough for the deposit.
nuance: Separable: put it by. British and slightly old-fashioned; put aside is more common now.
contrast: Put by saves money specifically; put aside can also mean setting a matter aside.

meaning: Formally apply or ask for something.
easyEnglish: Formally apply or ask for something.
japanese: 正式に申請する。願い出る。
cue: You want time off in August.
reply: I've put in for the first week of August.
transferCue: Describe applying for a transfer.
transferReply: She put in for a transfer to the Kyoto office.
nuance: Inseparable in this form; for introduces what is requested. It implies a formal process.
contrast: Put in for is a formal application; ask for is an ordinary request.

meaning: Have to explain your decisions to someone in authority.
easyEnglish: Have to explain your decisions to someone in authority.
japanese: 上の立場の人に、説明する義務を負う。
cue: A colleague asks who reviews your decisions.
reply: I account to the board twice a year.
transferCue: Describe a role with no oversight.
transferReply: He accounts to nobody, which is part of the problem.
nuance: Inseparable and formal. To introduces the person you answer to; for introduces what you explain.
contrast: Account to names who you report to; account for explains a cause or a total.

meaning: Change so that you fit a new situation.
easyEnglish: Change so that you fit a new situation.
japanese: 新しい状況に合わせて、自分を変える。
cue: A colleague has moved to a very different office.
reply: It took her a month to adapt to the new hours.
transferCue: Describe a plant in a new climate.
transferReply: These adapt to shade better than most.
nuance: Inseparable. Adapt something means changing the thing itself, not yourself.
contrast: Adapt to changes yourself to fit; get used to is about becoming comfortable.

meaning: Reach a shared decision about something.
easyEnglish: Reach a shared decision about something.
japanese: ある事柄について、双方が決着をつける。
cue: Two sides need to settle a date before anything else.
reply: Can we agree on a date before we discuss the budget?
transferCue: Describe a family settling a holiday.
transferReply: We finally agreed on the first week of August.
nuance: Inseparable. On introduces the matter settled; the people are the subject.
contrast: Agree on settles a matter; agree with shares an opinion; agree to accepts a proposal.

meaning: Say that something was caused by or created by someone.
easyEnglish: Say that something was caused by or created by someone.
japanese: 原因や作者を、それだと考える。
cue: A report explains a rise in demand. Summarise its claim.
reply: They attribute the increase to the winter campaign.
transferCue: Describe a painting of uncertain origin.
transferReply: The work is attributed to one of his students.
nuance: The effect goes between attribute and to, and the cause follows to. Often passive in writing.
contrast: Attribute to assigns a cause or author; put down to explains a cause more casually.

meaning: Use something as the foundation for a decision or a work.
easyEnglish: Use something as the foundation for a decision or a work.
japanese: それをよりどころにして、判断や作品を組み立てる。
cue: Explain where a forecast comes from.
reply: We based the forecast on three years of data.
transferCue: Describe a film's origin.
transferReply: The film is based on a diary found in an attic.
nuance: The work goes between base and on, and the source follows on. Very often passive: be based on.
contrast: Base on names the foundation; draw on means taking material from a source.

meaning: Rely on something happening.
easyEnglish: Rely on something happening.
japanese: そうなると見込んで、当てにする。
cue: A plan assumes good weather. Warn against it.
reply: I wouldn't bet on sunshine in March.
transferCue: Express confidence in a colleague.
transferReply: If anyone finishes on time, I'd bet on her.
nuance: Inseparable. Beyond gambling it means relying on an outcome, often in the negative.
contrast: Bet on expects an outcome; bank on is a firmer reliance you have planned around.

meaning: Reduce something to its essential point.
easyEnglish: Reduce something to its essential point.
japanese: 要点だけに、煮詰める。
cue: A long discussion has one real question. Name it.
reply: It boils down to whether we can afford the delay.
transferCue: Summarise a long report.
transferReply: Twenty pages boil down to one recommendation.
nuance: Usually with to and an abstract subject. The catalog also teaches boil down to as a whole.
contrast: Boil down finds the essential point; sum up restates the whole briefly.

meaning: Increase an amount, often suddenly.
easyEnglish: Increase an amount, often suddenly.
japanese: 数量や金額を、ぐっと引き上げる。
cue: A supplier raised a quoted price late in the process.
reply: They bumped up the price after we'd agreed the scope.
transferCue: Describe increasing an order.
transferReply: Could we bump up the order to fifty?
nuance: Separable: bump it up. Informal, and it suggests a noticeable jump rather than a gradual rise.
contrast: Bump up raises an amount; jack up implies the rise is unreasonable.

meaning: Suddenly start laughing or crying, or say something suddenly.
easyEnglish: Suddenly start laughing or crying, or say something suddenly.
japanese: 突然笑い出す・泣き出す。思わず口に出す。
cue: Describe a reaction to an unexpected joke.
reply: Half the room burst out laughing.
transferCue: Describe someone speaking without thinking.
transferReply: She burst out with the whole story.
nuance: Intransitive. Followed by an -ing verb for laughing and crying, or by with for speech.
contrast: Burst out is a sudden reaction; break down is losing composure over time.

meaning: Complete something despite difficulty, or support someone through it.
easyEnglish: Complete something despite difficulty, or support someone through it.
japanese: 困難のなかでもやり遂げる。支えて乗り切らせる。
cue: A plan survived a difficult year. Describe it.
reply: They carried the reform through despite the opposition.
transferCue: Describe what sustained someone.
transferReply: Her humour carried her through the worst month.
nuance: Separable: carry it through. Two senses: completing a plan, and sustaining a person.
contrast: Carry through completes a plan; follow through does what you promised afterwards.

meaning: Have something as the main subject or focus.
easyEnglish: Have something as the main subject or focus.
japanese: それを中心として据える。
cue: Explain what a discussion was mainly about.
reply: The debate centred on who pays for the repair.
transferCue: Describe a novel's subject.
transferReply: The story centres on two sisters in the 1930s.
nuance: Inseparable. British spells it centre, American center; both double the r in centred or not.
contrast: Centre on names the main subject; revolve around suggests everything else depends on it.

meaning: Think about something for a while before deciding.
easyEnglish: Think about something for a while before deciding.
japanese: しばらく噛みしめて考える。
cue: A colleague wants an answer you are not ready to give.
reply: Let me chew on it overnight.
transferCue: Offer someone time with a difficult question.
transferReply: Here's something to chew on before Friday.
nuance: Inseparable and informal, mostly American. Chew over is the closest British equivalent.
contrast: Chew on is unhurried thinking; sleep on it specifically means waiting until tomorrow.

meaning: Hold onto a belief or hope, often past the point of reason.
easyEnglish: Hold onto a belief or hope, often past the point of reason.
japanese: 望みや考えに、しがみつく。
cue: Someone still expects an outcome that is very unlikely.
reply: He clings to the idea that they'll call back.
transferCue: Describe holding onto a habit.
transferReply: She clings to the paper diary and always will.
nuance: Inseparable. Cling is irregular: clung. With beliefs it usually implies the hope is unrealistic.
contrast: Cling to holds on past reason; hang onto is neutral about keeping something.

meaning: Happen at the same time as something else, or disagree strongly.
easyEnglish: Happen at the same time as something else, or disagree strongly.
japanese: 予定がぶつかる。激しく対立する。
cue: Two meetings have been booked for the same hour.
reply: That clashes with the client call at two.
transferCue: Describe a disagreement between two managers.
transferReply: They clashed with each other over the budget.
nuance: Inseparable. The scheduling sense is common in British English; colours can clash too.
contrast: Clash with is a conflict of times or views; coincide with is a neutral overlap.

meaning: Approach a problem from a particular direction.
easyEnglish: Approach a problem from a particular direction.
japanese: ある角度から、問題に取り組む。
cue: A team is stuck and needs a different approach.
reply: Let's come at it from the customer's side instead.
transferCue: Describe two researchers with different methods.
transferReply: They come at the same question from opposite ends.
frame: Come at something from a direction
nuance: Inseparable, usually with from. A separate sense is being attacked, which context distinguishes.
contrast: Come at chooses an angle on a problem; go about is the method you use to do a task.

meaning: Result from something.
easyEnglish: Result from something.
japanese: その結果として生じる。
cue: A promising conversation produced no result.
reply: Nothing came of the meeting in the end.
transferCue: Describe an unexpected outcome.
transferReply: A lasting friendship came of that first project.
nuance: Inseparable. The result is the subject, and it is very often nothing: nothing came of it.
contrast: Come of names what resulted; come about explains how something happened.

meaning: Promise firmly to do something.
easyEnglish: Promise firmly to do something.
japanese: 確約する。責任を持って引き受ける。
cue: A client wants certainty about a date.
reply: I can commit to the fifteenth, not before.
transferCue: Describe someone who avoids firm promises.
transferReply: He never commits to anything in writing.
nuance: Inseparable, followed by a noun or -ing. Commit yourself to adds emphasis on personal obligation.
contrast: Commit to is a firm promise; lean towards is only a preference.

meaning: Say that one thing is like another.
easyEnglish: Say that one thing is like another.
japanese: あるものを、別のものにたとえる。
cue: You want to explain a new idea by likeness.
reply: I'd compare it to learning an instrument.
transferCue: Describe a reviewer's praise.
transferReply: The critic compared her to the great essayists.
nuance: The thing goes between compare and to. Compared to at the start of a sentence works for both senses.
contrast: Compare to likens two things; compare with examines their differences.

meaning: Make up for something missing or lost.
easyEnglish: Make up for something missing or lost.
japanese: 足りない分を、別のもので補う。
cue: A product is slower but much cheaper. Balance the two.
reply: The price compensates for the slower delivery.
transferCue: Describe adapting after an injury.
transferReply: He compensates for the knee with a shorter stride.
nuance: Inseparable. For introduces the shortfall. It can also mean paying someone for a loss.
contrast: Compensate for offsets a shortfall; make up for often repairs a personal failing.

meaning: Admit to something you feel awkward about.
easyEnglish: Admit to something you feel awkward about.
japanese: 気まずいことを、打ち明ける。
cue: You never finished a book everyone praised.
reply: I confess to never having finished it.
transferCue: Describe admitting a small mistake.
transferReply: She confessed to moving the file.
nuance: Inseparable, followed by a noun or -ing. Lighter than admit in everyday use, and often self-deprecating.
contrast: Confess to admits something awkward; own up to admits responsibility for a fault.

meaning: Tell someone private things because you trust them.
easyEnglish: Tell someone private things because you trust them.
japanese: 信頼して、内密なことを打ち明ける。
cue: A friend needs someone to talk to. Offer.
reply: You can confide in me if it helps.
transferCue: Describe a mentor relationship.
transferReply: She confided in her old tutor for years.
nuance: Inseparable; in introduces the trusted person. Confide something to someone names what is told.
contrast: Confide in trusts a person; open up describes becoming willing to share generally.

meaning: Have something as its essential quality.
easyEnglish: Have something as its essential quality.
japanese: 本質が、そこにある。
cue: Explain what really makes a job difficult.
reply: The difficulty consists in keeping everyone informed.
transferCue: Describe what makes a dish work.
transferReply: The trick consists in cooking it slowly.
nuance: Inseparable and formal. It names an essential quality, not the parts of a thing.
contrast: Consist in names the essence; consist of lists the parts something is made from.

meaning: Help to cause or improve something.
easyEnglish: Help to cause or improve something.
japanese: その一因となる。役立つ形で加わる。
cue: Several factors caused a delay. Name one.
reply: The late delivery contributed to the overrun.
transferCue: Describe someone's role in a project.
transferReply: Everyone contributed to the final version.
nuance: Inseparable. It suggests one factor among several, which makes it useful for careful writing.
contrast: Contribute to is partial causation; lead to points at a direct result.

meaning: Change into a different form or system.
easyEnglish: Change into a different form or system.
japanese: 別の形式や方式に変える。
cue: A file is in the wrong format for a client.
reply: Convert it to a PDF before you send it.
transferCue: Describe a building's change of use.
transferReply: The mill was converted to flats in the nineties.
nuance: The thing goes between convert and to. Into works equally well and is common with buildings.
contrast: Convert to changes form; change over switches from one system to another.

meaning: Exchange letters or messages with someone over time.
easyEnglish: Exchange letters or messages with someone over time.
japanese: 手紙やメールのやり取りを、長く続ける。
cue: Describe a long-distance friendship.
reply: They corresponded with each other for thirty years.
transferCue: Describe research into an archive.
transferReply: She corresponded with three museums about the letters.
nuance: Inseparable and slightly formal. Correspond with can also mean matching, which context separates.
contrast: Correspond with exchanges letters; correspond to means matching something.

meaning: Say that someone deserves recognition for something.
easyEnglish: Say that someone deserves recognition for something.
japanese: その功績を、その人のものと認める。
cue: One person's idea shaped a whole project.
reply: She's credited with the original idea.
transferCue: Give recognition in a speech.
transferReply: I credit the team with everything that worked.
nuance: The person goes between credit and with. Often passive: be credited with.
contrast: Credit with gives recognition; put down to explains a cause without praise.

meaning: Reduce something, or interrupt it.
easyEnglish: Reduce something, or interrupt it.
japanese: 取り分を削る。時間などに食い込む。
cue: A long meeting is eating into working time.
reply: These calls cut into the whole afternoon.
transferCue: Describe a fee affecting earnings.
transferReply: The charges cut into our margin badly.
nuance: Inseparable. Cut is irregular and unchanged: cut. Used for time, profit and savings.
contrast: Cut into takes a noticeable share; eat away at erodes gradually and unnoticed.

meaning: Have existed since a particular time.
easyEnglish: Have existed since a particular time.
japanese: その時代から存在している。
cue: A visitor asks how old a wall is.
reply: The wall dates from the fourteenth century.
transferCue: Describe a long-standing rule.
